title: Scaling the Next Paradigm of Heterogeneous Intelligence — Adrian Bertagnoli, Callosum

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk's central object is serving workloads across heterogeneous hardware (Cerebras, SambaNova, frontier APIs) with explicit latency/cost tradeoffs and a task-routing runtime, matching inference_model_systems. The paradigm is presented as a general compute shift, while Callosum's automation layer is a developer platform for routing tasks to optimal model/hardware combinations. Benchmark case studies are research-grade validations, while the Callosum automation layer is a prototype-stage platform under active construction with grant funding. Assumes familiarity with neural scaling laws, MoE, pre-fill/decode disaggregation, recursive language models, and production-function formalization. A 15-minute conference presentation with slides, two case studies, and a Q&A segment. All supporting anchors are grade 'said_in_transcript' with no external artifacts or code available.

summary: Adrian Bertagnoli introduces heterogeneous intelligence as the successor to the homogeneous paradigm of scaling single models on fleets of identical chips, a paradigm rooted in neural scaling laws from the training domain that becomes less relevant as inference dominates. He identifies three stages of heterogeneity: mild (current—MoE architectures, multi-agent systems, pre-fill/decode disaggregation on homogeneous clusters), moderate (different chips for different models, state-space and diffusion models interacting), and full (co-evolution of hardware and software with vertical integration). The rationale is that real-world problems are complex, multi-step, and open-ended, decomposing into sub-problems requiring vastly different intelligences. Callosum formalizes this as the principle of maximum heterogeneity, showing that under reasonable constraints heterogeneous systems outperform homogeneous ones—a trend observed across neuroscience, economics, and ecology. Practically, Callosum optimizes multi-agent systems at three levels: hardware selection, agent interaction, and workflow construction. The first case study extends recursive language models (from MIT) by mapping sub-context to different chips and models. On the Ulong benchmark, Cerebras yields 7x cheaper and 5x faster than frontier models; SambaNova achieves 12x cheaper and 3x faster, both matching accuracy. The second case study tackles visual web navigation on Video Web Arena. A mixture of Qwen 3 VL8B-Instruct and Kimi K2.5 beats GPT 5.2 and Gemini 2.5 by 18% and 25% respectively, while being 3.7x cheaper and 3x faster. Key to this success was offloading subtasks like zooming and visual parsing to smaller models, yielding 11x speed and 43x cost improvements on those steps alone. Looking ahead, Bertagnoli frames three eras of compute: CPU (faster), GPU/parallel (Nvidia-dominated), and heterogeneous (multi-agent workloads mapped to optimal chips). Callosum received a £3M grant from the UK's Aria institute for the first heterogeneous collocated cluster in the UK. In Q&A, he explains that task routing evolved from bespoke decisions to an automation layer that detects task complexity and predicts the best model and hardware.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and definition of heterogeneous intelligence
sections.summary: Bertagnoli introduces himself as a founding engineer at Callosum and outlines the talk: why heterogeneity matters for scaling AI, how it is used today, and how to utilize it in the future.

sections.title: Limitations of homogeneous intelligence and evolution toward heterogeneity
sections.summary: Homogeneous intelligence scales single models on identical chips, rooted in neural scaling laws from the training domain. As inference dominates, this becomes less relevant. Mild heterogeneity already exists through MoE architectures, multi-agent systems, and pre-fill/decode disaggregation. Bertagnoli describes three stages: mild (current), moderate (different chips for different models, state-space and diffusion models interacting), and full (co-evolution of hardware and software with vertical integration).

sections.title: Rationale and mathematical formalization of heterogeneity
sections.summary: Real-world problems are complex, multi-step, and open-ended, decomposing into sub-problems requiring different intelligences. Scaling a singular intelligence is inefficient. Callosum formalized the principle of maximum heterogeneity using a production function over a skill space, showing that under reasonable constraints heterogeneous systems outperform homogeneous ones—a trend consistent across neuroscience, economics, and ecology.

sections.title: Practical implementation of heterogeneous workflows
sections.summary: Callosum optimizes multi-agent systems at three levels: hardware (choosing different hardware based on computational demands), agent interaction, and workflow construction. Two key primitives are introduced: heterogeneous recursion at the workflow level and multimodal video action language models at the agent layer.

sections.title: Recursive language models and Ulong benchmark results
sections.summary: Recursive language models (from MIT) treat context as an environment rather than putting it all into a prompt, addressing context rot where information requirements scale linearly or quadratically. Callosum extended this by mapping sub-context to different chips and models. On the Ulong benchmark, Cerebras achieved 7x cheaper and 5x faster than GPT 5.2; SambaNova achieved 12x cheaper and 3x faster, both matching accuracy.

sections.title: Visual web navigation and Video Web Arena performance
sections.summary: A mixture of Qwen 3 VL8B-Instruct and Kimi K2.5 beat GPT 5.2 and Gemini 2.5 on Video Web Arena by 18% and 25% respectively. The mixture was 1.3x faster than Kimi alone and 18x cheaper than GPT 5.2 alone. With Qwen 3 plus GPT, results were 3x faster and 3.7x cheaper. Offloading subtasks like zooming and visual parsing to smaller models yielded 11x speed and 43x cost improvements on those steps with no downside.

sections.title: Future of compute, Aria partnership, and closing summary
sections.summary: Bertagnoli frames three eras of compute: CPU (faster), GPU/parallel (Nvidia-dominated), and heterogeneous (multi-agent workloads mapped to optimal chips). Callosum received a £3M grant from the UK's Aria institute for the first heterogeneous collocated cluster in the UK. He closes by stating every new source of diversity makes the whole system smarter, faster, and cheaper.

sections.title: Q&A: Automation layer for task routing
sections.summary: Bertagnoli explains that task routing evolved from bespoke decisions mapping simple subtasks to simple models, to an automation layer that detects task complexity and automatically predicts the best suited model and hardware.
